outcome: wound complications (cellulitis, abscess, hematoma, seroma, or dehiscence)
cohort: 423 patients with class III obesity undergoing cesarean at their institution from 2010 to 2013 with singletons ≥ 34 weeks gestation
finding: In women with class III obesity, cesarean delivery via vertical abdominal incisions was associated with more maternal complications but fewer immediate neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery via vertical abdominal incisions was associated with an increased risk of vertical hysterotomy, decreased risk of 5-minute Apgar < 7, and not statistically significantly associated with transfusion or umbilical artery pH < 7.1.
